instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Fluent in Nonsense
cards.instruction: Perform complete mastery of the strange logic while inventing each rule only when it becomes necessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we price this bottled cloud, measure its third elbow. Bring the result to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm your new assistant. It only has two. May I open the bottle?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may address it first. 'Professor' is sufficient; the third elbow appears only for respectful staff.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Professor. It's raining now. Shall I stop?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Continue. Those are its credentials, and I decide when they're sufficient. Count ten drops through the glass and write the price. Any more and we'll be selling an overqualified cloud.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave your sofa on the ceiling until I say otherwise. Which way did you turn the gravity dial?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Right. My landlord arrives in ten minutes. Can I turn it back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One number. Slowly. The dial accepts a correction only when I have finished saying its name. Six.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six clicked, but the armchairs are rising. Can we stop naming numbers?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can. The chairs have requested a hearing. You explain the sofa; I'll hear their objections one at a time. Nobody turns anything while I'm listening.

cards.title: Raise the Impossibility
cards.instruction: Answer every strange offer with a more committed version that you can still justify.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For my restaurant, your flying chair must come with a flying table. Dinner travels with the diner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can make the table circle the room. Would that suit you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only with a hovering waiter. I won't have my customers calling down for soup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The waiter can serve upside down. Shall I put that in the quote?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Include gravity-proof soup before you send it. I decide the menu, and turning customers over between courses is not on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your invisible friend can bring her family to my wedding. Tell them I've set places beside me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They walk through walls when they're bored. Are you sure?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They can wander. I'll book a ballroom that follows them; my guests aren't missing cake because a wall got in the way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ballroom can split when they go different ways. Do you want that option?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take it, and order a cake that multiplies with the rooms. Everyone beside me gets the first slice; we'll need enough versions of me to cut them.

cards.title: Every Glitch Is a Gift
cards.instruction: Turn every contradiction or failure into a surprising benefit of the impossible system.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our garden door opens into the broom cupboard. Take a brush for the picnic crumbs; we'll use the route it gives us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now it's the attic. Can I put the sandwiches down and try the front door?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep them with you. This route saves us carrying the picnic blanket downstairs. Take it from that shelf.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now we're at the cellar. The sandwiches are getting warm. Are we eating here?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We are. Put them beside the wine to cool. This door has found us a picnic with a roof and a wine list. You choose the bottle; I'll choose when we leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The office clock is taking us backward. Leave it running; I intend to arrive at that meeting on time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've gone past the invitation. Can I stop it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not yet. We have preparation time now. Bring me the agenda when it exists.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're before the booking. The boss is asking me whether we need the meeting. What do I say?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her I've decided we don't. This clock has cleared everyone's afternoon. Put that in your reply, and copy me so she knows who to thank.

cards.title: Calm About the Impossible
cards.instruction: Remain perfectly calm around impossible events while becoming increasingly alarmed by ordinary details.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Your dragon can stay for tea. Please keep the biscuit crumbs off my carpet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His three heads breathe fire. Should I take him outside?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. He's fine here. Wait, three mouths? I need three napkins immediately.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He brought his own. They're paper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Paper? At my good table? Fetch the linen before the neighbors see.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The table can float while we pack. That wet cup needs a mat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's at the ceiling. Can I pull it down?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. You'll slide the cup across the polish. Get the stepladder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll climb up. I've still got my muddy boots on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Boots off! Socks too if they're damp. We are not adding footprints to that water ring.

cards.title: Impossible Currency
cards.instruction: Price every favor in symbolic acts, imaginary resources, or promises that cannot be measured normally.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may borrow my ladder until Friday. Leave your shadow with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need it at work. Could you take something else?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep its office hours. I'll have the evenings. Those are the terms; the ladder is yours when you agree.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. Could you hold it too? I'm afraid of heights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For that, leave me your fear of falling. I'll hold both until you're down. You can collect the fear afterward if you still want it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll repair your kettle for a spoonful of yesterday. Put your payment on the bench.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I pay with the five minutes I wasted this morning?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll allow wasted time. Useful time would complicate the repair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: But this morning is today. Will you still take it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave it overnight. I set the credit terms here: you get the kettle tomorrow, when your five minutes have become yesterday. No spending them while they mature.
